Performers
Lambert Murphy (tenor), Stefano Di Stefano (harp), William Carlino (lute) Documented

DAHR identifies Raymond Dixon as Murphy’s pseudonym, not a second singer. Di Stefano is credited for takes 3–⁠4; Francis J. Lapitino belongs only to discarded takes 1–⁠2 and is not credited on this issued take.

[1] [3] [2] [4]
Work version
Two songs from J.-B. Weckerlin’s Échos du temps passé, volume I, performed with harp and lute Documented

The label numbers Machaut’s Douce dame jolie first and Janequin’s L’espoir que j’ai second; DAHR quotes the collection title and volume from Victor’s ledgers. BnF describes the published collection as voice with piano, so the precise harp-and-lute adaptation is not established from that score.

[1] [3] [6]
Recorded
1915-03-17 Documented

Take 4 was made on 17 March 1915. The earlier matrix date 14 January 1915 refers to destroyed takes 1–⁠2, not the recording streamed here.

[3] [2] [4]
Place
New York, New York, United States Documented

DAHR specifies New York for takes 3–⁠4. Camden belongs to the January takes and is not substituted for this session; the studio address is unknown.

[3] [2] [4]
Label
Victor Talking Machine Company; blue label Documented

The viewed label names Victor and Lambert Murphy and specifies tenor with harp and lute, in French.

[1] [4]
Catalogue
45083-B, 10-inch disc Documented

The side suffix B is visible on the label. LOC and DAHR identify the 10-inch carrier.

[1] [3] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
B-15595, take 4; side 45083-B Documented

DAHR marks take 4 as Master and links the same audio. Matrix/take identification comes from discographic records, not from claiming to read an illegible run-out inscription.

[3] [2] [1] [4]
Transfer
Source disc: UCSB Davidson Library, Department of Special Collections; National Jukebox digital access; Hessel Digital Library mirror Documented

LOC identifies the source collection. The mirror credits digitisation to the Library of Congress Packard Campus; DAHR also describes the audio as from the UCSB Library. No individual transfer engineer is established.

[2] [5]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The original disc-transfer date is unknown. The Archive mirror states LOC retrieval on 30 September 2026 and repository publication on 10 October 2026; neither is the 1915 session or 1916 release.

[2] [5]
Processing
Archive describes its MP3 as a bit-exact copy of the LOC-served MP3, with no processing Documented

This records the mirror’s provenance statement, not an independently performed checksum comparison. Original stylus, speed correction, equalisation and noise-reduction settings are unknown. No additional audio cut is made.

[5] [2]
Composition rights
Historical songs and Weckerlin collection are outside ordinary composition copyright terms Inferred, not documented

BnF gives Weckerlin’s dates 1821–⁠1910 and the collection’s publication in 1853–⁠1857. The exact person responsible for adapting its piano accompaniment to harp and lute is not established. Recording admission rests independently on the documented pre-cutoff publication.

[6] [1]
Recording rights
Rule 2 — United States public domain: published May 1916 Documented

Victor 45083’s documented 1916 publication precedes the project’s 1925 cutoff. source.rights uses us-published-before-cutoff with published 1916. The Archive Public Domain Mark is corroborative, not the sole basis; its 1915 first-publication claim and simplified statutory explanation are not repeated. This is a US basis, not a claim of worldwide clearance.

[4] [1] [3] [2] [5]

Machaut, Douce dame jolie, and Janequin, L’espoir que j’ai, from Weckerlin’s Échos du temps passé; Lambert Murphy, tenor, Stefano Di Stefano, harp, William Carlino, lute. Recorded New York, 17 March 1915; Victor 45083-B, matrix B-15595, take 4; released May 1916. Source disc UCSB; Library of Congress, National Jukebox; Hessel Digital Library mirror on Internet Archive. US public-domain recording. Rights statement

  3. DAHR — Victor matrix B-15595, Douce dame jolie — Personnel, pseudonym note, Weckerlin title note and take table: takes 1–⁠2 Camden January 1915; takes 3–⁠4 New York March 1915; take 4 master, Victor 45083.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. John R. Bolig, The Victor Discography: Green, Blue, and Purple Labels — Blue Label (10-inch), entry 45083, printed p. 32: B-15595-4, 17-Mar-15 session, May-16 release, New York. Introduction distinguishes recording from release dates.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
